requirements.evidence: Contract largely met: migrations with cascading FKs, unique (entity_id, slug)/(queue_id, code) and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:16-28); Queue/Ticket models with the specified casts and relations (Queue.php:160-187, Ticket.php:224-266); enums, InactiveQueueException, IssueTicket with priority guard (IssueTicket.php:41-43), a locked fresh re-read inside the transaction (IssueTicket.php:50-54) and up to 5 retries on 23000; write-once updating guard (Ticket.php:246-255); call() with membership and status checks (Ticket.php:289-307); factories with forQueue (TicketFactory.php:382-387). Gaps: nextCode takes the numeric max of all valid codes rather than the 'last valid code by insertion order' (Ticket.php:276-280; the orderBy('id') has no effect). call() does a check-then-save without a lock or conditional update, so two concurrent calls can both pass the Waiting check and break the single-call invariant (Ticket.php:291-306).

conventions.evidence: Docs kept in sync (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md). Fillable attributes are set deliberately, the domain write goes through App\Actions\IssueTicket, migrations have a reversible down(), and the style matches siblings (casts() method, #[Fillable], factory PHPDoc). Deviation: authorization in Ticket::call is a hand-rolled membership check (`! $user->membershipFor($entityId)`, Ticket.php:299) instead of a policy/gate, while the conventions require authorization 'always goes through policies/gates'. The contract does require call() on the model.

security.evidence: call() authorizes server-side against the entity membership resolved from the DB (Ticket.php:297-301), and the non-member test confirms the ticket is unchanged (TicketCallTest.php:808-816). Issuance re-reads the queue under lockForUpdate (IssueTicket.php:50). Mass assignment is restricted via #[Fillable]. Limited gap: call() has no row lock or `where status = waiting` conditional update, so a race can double-call a ticket and overwrite called_by_user_id.

tests.evidence: Pest tests cover: defaults, explicit priority/channel, A999->A1000->A1001, deleted number not reused, malformed codes, inactive queue, stale instance, negative priority (IssueTicketTest.php); schema, cascades, factory behaviour, forQueue sequencing, explicit codes (QueueTicketSchemaTest.php); call happy path, double call, non-member, write-once (TicketCallTest.php). Missing: no test for the unique-collision retry path, and no case where insertion order and numeric max differ (which would expose the nextCode semantics).

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall with no extra layers. However, nextCode plucks every code in the queue on each issuance and scans it in PHP (Ticket.php:276), which is O(n) per ticket and grows without bound. The `catch (InactiveQueueException $e) { throw $e; }` (IssueTicket.php:65-66) is redundant because that exception is not a QueryException.

readability.evidence: Clear names, a MUTABLE_AFTER_ISSUANCE constant, and helpful PHPDoc on public methods. Nits: `\LogicException` is fully qualified inline while AuthorizationException is imported (Ticket.php:251, 294); there is a redundant rethrow catch; and orderBy('id') suggests insertion-order semantics that the max() loop does not implement.

scope.evidence: All files serve the task: models, enums, exception, action, factories, migrations, tests and the required doc and changelog updates. No HTTP, Livewire or call-next code was added.

issues.explanation: call() checks status after refresh() and then saves, with no lock or conditional update, so two concurrent calls can both succeed and break the 'called exactly once' invariant.

nextCode uses the numeric max of all valid codes instead of the last valid code by insertion order as specified, which makes the orderBy('id') ineffective; the two give different results when a lower code is inserted after a higher one.
Every issuance loads all codes of the queue into PHP; a query for the latest valid row would avoid this unbounded O(n) cost.
Authorization is a hand-rolled membership check in the model rather than going through a policy/gate as the conventions require.
No test exercises the unique (queue_id, code) collision retry path, or a case that distinguishes insertion order from numeric max.
SQLSTATE 23000 covers every integrity violation (e.g. FK failures), not just unique collisions, so unrelated constraint errors are also retried.
Catching InactiveQueueException only to rethrow it is dead code.
LogicException is referenced fully qualified inline while other exceptions are imported, which is inconsistent.

review.summary: The change adds queues/tickets migrations, models, enums, factories, the IssueTicket action with a locked re-read and collision retry, write-once and single-call guards, thorough Pest tests, and updated docs and changelog. It is solid and well scoped, but Ticket::call is not concurrency-safe for the single-call invariant, nextCode uses numeric max rather than insertion order and scans every code per issuance, and authorization bypasses the policy convention, so I would approve with requested follow-ups.
